notes.title: CTHON Update - 4/12/2022
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

After far too long, CTHON has finally been updated to the Game Maker Studio 2 engine from Game Maker 8.1!

This has been all about making sure the source code doesn't sit there and rot and that the game continues to be stable on newer OSs. A few minor bugs have been fixed here and there, but it's the same game you all know and hopefully love. Theoretically, the game should be much more performative because it is compiled with the YoYo Compiler rather than interpreted.

Please let me know if you encounter any issues with the update.

Sorry it took such a long time to update CTHON, and thank you for sticking with me.

Gravity

notes.title: Patch Notes for 1-21-18
notes.content:
Hi everyone,

Just a quick patch to fix a bug:

[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*] Fixed a bug where an error would be thrown on the final score screen (after defeating the final boss) if the game was saved and exited right before the final boss level.
[/list]

Note: If you notice the file sizes are hundreds of megabytes, don't be alarmed; because of the way Game Maker works, I have to overwrite the executable entirely whenever I recompile the game with code changes. Download sizes for CTHON at the moment should be right around 244 MB, though that number will  slowly rise as additional code is added.

notes.title: Patch Notes - 10-3-2017
notes.content:
Hey all! Here is what is new to CTHON:

[h1]Balance Changes[/h1]
[list]
[*] Revamped item spawning to be more forgiving, especially on later levels. Resource items (health, ammo, and grenades) reduce less rapidly per level. This is most noticeable in the late game. Each difficulty is different in how rapidly it reduces item count per level; Beginner has a flatter curve, while Hardcore has a steeper curve. Item spawning is still random, but generally not as scarce.
[*] Revamped the way secrets spawn so that they have less of an overall impact on the game; some secrets can still contain very good loot, not so good loot, and even monsters, but there are now far less secrets on any given level and they more frequently spawn in larger blank areas instead of on obscure corners.
[*] The player now starts with two inventory slots instead of just one.
[/list]

[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*] Fixed a bug where the score screen would start to incorrectly report the number of total secrets found if you started a new run without closing the application.
[/list]

[h1]Other Changes[/h1]
[list]
[*] Changed the game's font to something more legible and less wide.
[*] Added seams to the textures of secret walls to make them easier to find.
[/list]

Thanks and have fun!

notes.title: Patch Notes - 4/17/2017
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

This update has come early due to a crash bug that needed fixing. Here is what is new in CTHON:

[h1]New Features[/h1]
[list]
[*]Added a new item (this was originally planned for the May update) - Large Nanite Unit. This item provides 25 nanites. This is a subtle change, but it should allow you to be a little more liberal with spending nanites.
[/list]

[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*]Fixed a crash bug related to audio playback issues on Windows 8 and Windows 8.1, caused by Wyrm enemies.
[/list]

[h1]Known Issues[/h1]
[list]
[*]Alt Tabbing causes the Strafe On control (when mapped to Alt, which is the default) to stick. A workaround is to tap Alt again when you refocus on the game window.
[/list]

Thank you, and enjoy!

notes.title: CTHON - Patch Notes - 4/7/2017
notes.content:
Hi everyone!

Here is what is new in CTHON:

[h1]New Features[/h1]
[list]
[*]The game can now run in a window. Use F4 at any time to toggle between windowed and fullscreen modes. You can also Alt-Tab out as well as resize the window by dragging the edges.
[*]The game now has one resolution mode for launch (an emulated 640x480 display); the forced 640x480 mode was causing more problems than it was worth. Higher resolutions are planned for a later patch. This may cause display issues with certain recording software, so if you plan to record gameplay you may need to configure your software for window capture.
[*]Added a "Strafe On" key that defaults to Alt. Holding this key allows you to use Turn Left and Turn Right to strafe in the corresponding direction. Ideal for old-school keyboard setups.
[*]Added back in a brief overview of the controls. A message at the beginning of the game displays to inform players to use F1 for a list of controls.
[*]Added extra sounds for weapons equipped with several damage upgrades.
[*]Added a new type of map piece.
[*]Changed the way health, ammo, and bombs display - they are now displayed in an x/x form.
[/list]

[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*]Fixed a bug where mapping a control to one of the mouse buttons would cause every key to perform that action.
[*]Fixed a bug where saving and exiting would not record the total time of the run accurately.
[/list]

[h1]Balancing[/h1]
[list]
[*]Rebalanced the way items spawn. In particular, the previous version was spawning too many Framework Nodes to be practical.
[*]Removed items in the final boss fight. The reason for this was to increase the level of tension at the end of the game and require some planning on the player’s part. 
[*]The Blade now deals higher base damage for all classes (and the Berserker still starts with more than the other classes). This will hopefully make melee a little more viable.
[*]Berserker now starts with slightly faster base speed.
[*]Sapper now starts with slightly faster launcher fire rate.
[/list]

Thank you, and enjoy!

EDIT: The next major update will be planned for between May 5 and May 12, 2017. Please don't hesitate to report bugs in the Bug Reports section of the forum, and request new features in the Feature Requests section! Generally, large features must be planned for the following patch, but small things that are relatively easy to implement can usually be bumped up the list, and of course, major bugs always take high priority. I will also be looking at implementing Achievements for this month. Thanks again!

notes.title: CTHON - Patch Schedule
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

Thank you for all your feedback so far. It's pretty exhilarating to see the game finally on Steam after what seemed like such a long time.

I wanted to take the opportunity to let everyone know how changes to CTHON will work over the next few months. My intention is to go with the industry-standard: one main patch every four weeks. Four weeks will hopefully give me enough time to sort through bug reports, feature requests, optimizations and improvements, while at the same time providing me with time to work on other things (and be able to live a life outside the game!).

I am still deciding where to start that timeline; I may try to get the first main patch (which I'm working on currently) out on about March 31 or April 1. This one will include the most pressing fixes - eliminating bugs and troubleshooting any performance issues. If that timeline doesn't work out then I will push it to about the 7th of April (I'll be on a vacation the week of the 10th).

The way patches will work after that is that I will keep a backlog of bug reports and feature requests, and anything reported/requested while working on the current patch will then be planned for the next patch. I'm flexible though; if there is something totally game breaking I will move that up the priority list.

I hope that made sense - if you have any questions feel free to ask.

Thanks!
